messages:
ella.cs: Heads up — Acme reported elevated latencies and a handful of 5xxs this morning between 08:12–08:26 UTC on Dedicated pool eu-west-1. They say it started after our 07:55 deploy. Can we page SRE? I’m on the call with their TAM.
ajay.eng: Thanks Ella. I can take first pass. Paging @tom.sre and @oncall-bot — please escalate to SRE on-call.
oncall-bot: Incident alert created: INC-20240315-8472 — high p50/p95 latency and 502 errors on /v1/generate for model redwood-1-large-dedicated. Notifying: tom.sre, ryan.eng. Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-20240315-8472
tom.sre: I’m on it. Starting triage — checking deploy logs and autoscaler metrics. Ella can you paste the Acme error samples and timestamps you have?
ella.cs: Pasting logs from Acme (redacted):
```
2024-03-15T08:12:07Z acme: request_id=abc123 status=200 latency_ms=420
2024-03-15T08:13:19Z acme: request_id=abc456 status=502 backend_err=kvcache_miss
2024-03-15T08:14:01Z acme: request_id=abc789 status=502 timeout_ms=30000
```
They reported ~3–5% of requests failing, p95 spiking to ~1.2s from usual ~120ms.
ryan.eng: Noted. I’m pulling runtime traces and kernel selection logs. Quick hypothesis: the deploy included a quantized kernel update — could be a cache flush interaction causing KV-cache thrash.
tom.sre: Confirming spike aligns with deploy. Autoscaler shows a small transient pod restart (~07:56) and increased retry rates. Rolling back the deploy is a safe mitigation if we see correlation. ajay, can you prepare rollback? I’ll keep working on root cause.
ajay.eng: Preparing rollback. Command I’ll run:
```
redwoodctl deploy rollback --service=inference-dedicated --revision=20240314-99
```
ETA ~5m to start traffic switching.
elia.cs: small typo — I’m on customer call and they want a status page blurb and a short email we can send Ops/TAM. Can we draft both? We should avoid blame, focus on impact and next steps.
kate.support: Draft status page suggestion:
```
Incident: Elevated latencies and increased 502 errors affecting some Dedicated customers in eu-west-1
Start time: 2024-03-15 08:12 UTC
Impact: A subset of requests for model redwood-1-large-dedicated may experience increased latency or 502 errors. Mitigation: We are rolling back a recent runtime change and monitoring. Next update: in 15 minutes.
```
liz.ops: Good — keep the language customer-focused. Also add the affected API path (/v1/generate) and a note we will follow up with affected customers directly.
ajay.eng: Rollback initiated. Switching traffic back to revision 20240314-99 now. Watch logs for warmup.
oncall-bot: Rollback deployment triggered by ajay.eng at 2201234575. Status: in progress.
tom.sre: After rollback started, error rate dropped to baseline within ~90s. Preliminary mitigation successful. I’ll let SRE continue validation for 10 min before we close the incident.
ryan.eng: Observed that the changed kernel caused cold-KV-cache path to handle more memory and triggered retries on some requests until the cache warmed. Rollback removes the new kernel path. Long-term fix: we need a rolling warmup step and stricter canary (traffic ramp) for kernel-level changes.
ella.cs: Great, please help craft a short customer-facing note I can send to Acme’s TAM. They want timeline, impact, and next steps (including credit and mitigation).
kate.support: Draft customer email (short):
```
Hi Sam,

Quick update: Earlier today (2024-03-15 08:12–08:26 UTC) you may have seen increased latency and occasional 502 errors for requests served by the Dedicated eu-west-1 pool. Root cause: a runtime kernel update deployed at 07:55 UTC that interacted poorly with KV cache warmup. Mitigation: we rolled back the deploy at ~08:16 UTC and error rates returned to baseline within ~2 minutes.

Impact: ~3–5% of requests experienced errors; p95 latency temporarily increased to ~1.2s. We’ll follow up with a full RCA and the preventative actions below. We’re happy to discuss SLA credits — please let me know how you’d like us to proceed.

Next steps we’re tracking:
- Full RCA and timeline by 2024-03-16 EOD
- Improved canary/ramp for kernel changes + automatic warmup step
- Proactive rollback automation for similar regressions

Thanks,
Ella (Redwood CS)
```
tom.sre: +1 to that. For internal RCA summary to paste into the post-incident doc:
```
Summary: Runtime kernel update introduced a new code path for quantized execution. Under Dedicated workload with cold KV cache, this caused increased memory pressure and retries on KV requests, producing transient 502s and latency spikes. Mitigation: rollback to previous kernel removed the regression. Corrective actions: add warmup traffic step, strengthen canary thresholds for kernel-level changes, add telemetry to detect KV cache thrash patterns and trigger automated rollback.
```
ryan.eng: I’ll follow up with a proposed experiment to run kernel change tests against synthetic cold-cache workloads and add a warmup hook into the deploy pipeline.
ajay.eng: Logging done, incident marked as mitigated. Please confirm capture of timeline and customer comms so CS can send.
elia.cs: Small timeline clarification I need before I send: exact rollback time and when error rates returned to baseline (for Acme’s TAM). We have approximate times above but please confirm precise timestamps.
tom.sre: Rollback command issued at 2024-03-15T08:16:15Z. Error rate returned to baseline at 2024-03-15T08:18:40Z (per Prometheus p95 and 502 count). Add buffer note: customers started seeing improvements within ~90–150s after rollback began.
kate.support: Thanks — I’ll send the note now and copy engineering. I’ll also offer a meeting if Acme wants a deeper walkthrough.
elia.cs: Also tagging next action owners:
- RCA writeup & postmortem doc: tom.sre (due 2024-03-16 EOD)
- Deploy pipeline warmup & canary changes: ryan.eng (proposal due 2024-03-20)
- Customer credit and follow-up call: ella.cs (coordinate with Sam/TAM)
- Observability alert for KV thrash: ajay.eng (add rule + runbook)
liz.ops: Recommend we also add a scheduled customer-facing postmortem to status page once the RCA is ready. Good job triaging everyone. :+1:
ryan.eng: I’ll attach the preliminary traces and a short log excerpt to the postmortem doc.
elia.cs: Sending to Acme now. Will post any reply here. Thank you team — great coordination.

-- end of thread --
